text:
Amy Chen: Quick heads-up — FalconCare (healthcare analytics) is asking for a bespoke discount for a private/on-prem POC. They want 45% off list for a 6mo pilot and then convert to a 12mo dedicated commit if POC is successful. Also requesting SOC2 evidence and a short on-site audit window. Are we able to approve the 45% for the POC?

Jamie Park: Do we have the expected committed $s if they convert to Dedicated? Need to model margin impact before approving anything >35%.

Rishi Patel: On my call with their CFO — they said they'd sign a 12mo dedicated at roughly $60k/mo ARR if we include migration credits and a conversion credit that applies to the first 3 months of the commit. The 6mo POC is strictly reduced-rate; they'd like the POC pricing to be separate and not count toward the commit unless conversion happens.

Tina Gomez: From SE/security side — they pushed an infosec questionnaire and asked about data residency + evidence of SOC2 Type II. We can host in their VPC/private deploy but need legal to confirm permissibility of on-site audit and to provide SOC2 documentation. Also, for on-prem they want a short maintenance window guarantee during the POC.

sec-bot: Automated sec checklist: SOC2 docs available via customer-portal link; formal evidence release requires NDA + signed DPA. Raised ticket SEC-2026-117 for ATO path.

Dan Morales: Financial constraints: standard floor for enterprise POC discounts is 15–30% depending on commit signal. We allow up to 35% if there's a clear committed uplift (signed MOU / financial commit). Anything >35% requires VP Sales + RevOps approval and a margin protection plan. 45% looks risky unless the total contract value (TCV) post-conversion is >= $720k (i.e., $60k/mo * 12 = $720k) AND we get an explicit conversion clause that rolls POC credits into the commit. Without that, margin falls below acceptable.

Dan Morales: Example calc (rough):
```
List rate estimate (hosted equiv): $0.10 per 1k units (example pricing bucket)
Estimated token volume POC: 40M tokens/mo -> ~$4k at list -> POC monthly revenue at 45% off = $2,200 (too low)
If convert to dedicated @ $60k/mo then 45% overall discount can be absorbed only if conversion is signed before POC ends and credits expire into the committed term.
```

Jamie Park: Proposal: approve a conditional POC discount of 30% for 6mo, with a 20% conversion credit applied to the first 3 months of the 12mo dedicated if they sign within 30 days post-POC. Add milestone-based success credits (e.g., +5% credits after defined perf/uptime gates). That keeps us within margins and gives the customer an incentive to convert.

Rishi Patel: FalconCare will push back on 30% — they're negotiating with another vendor offering aggressive pilot pricing. If we don't give 40–45 they'll likely ask for extra migration/support credits. Can we escalate for a one-time 40% on the POC if they sign a non-cancellable 12mo commit at $60k/mo within 14 days of POC end?

Amy Chen: Tagging Derek for escalation: @Derek Liu (VP Sales) — can you weigh in? They want 45% conditional on a fast convert clause and audit accommodations. Also need clarity on whether the SOC2 evidence + DPA can be turned around in 7–10 business days.

Derek Liu (VP Sales): Thanks — this is a standard negotiation profile. I'm okay to approve up to 40% POC discount ONLY if we get a signed, non-cancellable conversion LOI committing to the $60k/mo for 12 months and we capture acceptance milestones (so credits are clawed back if conversion doesn't happen). 45% is our outlier and needs CRO sign-off; not comfortable with 45% pre-approval. Also loop in Legal to accelerate SOC2/DPA.

Amy Chen: Sounds good. I'll counter with Jamie's structure: 30% now, 20% conversion credit, escalation path to 40% with signed LOI inside 14 days. I'll also open the SEC ticket for the DPA + SOC2 request and notify Legal.

Tina Gomez: I'll prep the POC runbook with the uptime/milestone gates and the on-site window language so Legal can see exact asks.

Rishi Patel: OK — I'll present the counter to FalconCare and push for the 40% shortcut. If they insist on 45% I'll request time to get CRO sign-off but no promise.

Jamie Park: I'll draft the MOU sketch and a margin impact summary for RevOps to sign off quickly.

Amy Chen: Thanks everyone — next steps: Jamie drafts MOU, Tina drafts runbook, sec-bot/Legal to provide SOC2/DPA turn-around ETA. I'll update thread with the customer's response. :thumbsup:
